definitions.meaning: Distance travelled per unit time, calculated as distance divided by time, measured in metres per second.
Speed with a direction: displacement divided by time, so a round trip back to the start has zero average velocity.
The straight-line change in position from start to finish, with a direction - not the total path length.
The rate of change of velocity, read off a velocity-time graph as its gradient.
Rise over run on a graph: on a distance-time graph it is the speed, and on a velocity-time graph it is the acceleration.
The product of velocity and time accumulated under the line, which equals the distance travelled.

mechanismSteps: Velocity is speed with a direction: the athlete covers 100 metres in 20 seconds for a speed of 5 metres per second, and running right makes it a velocity of 5 metres per second rightwards.
Distance-time graphs: the line climbs 120 metres in 60 seconds and the gradient triangle builds beneath it - gradient is rise over run, 120 over 60, a speed of 2 metres per second.

Velocity-time graphs: the line rises from 0 to 20 metres per second in 10 seconds, so the slope is an acceleration of 2 metres per second squared, while the shaded area growing under the line is the 100 metres travelled.
Check the thinking: the runner covers 800 metres in 100 seconds for a speed of 8 metres per second, but ends at the start, so displacement and velocity are both zero.
objectives: Calculate speed from distance and time, and velocity from displacement and time
Read the gradient of a distance-time graph as speed
Read the gradient of a velocity-time graph as acceleration and the area underneath as distance travelled
subject: science
title: Motion: speed, velocity and graphs

trap.explanation: Flat reads as "nothing is happening", so the line feels like zero movement. A flat v-t line means constant velocity: the object keeps moving at the same speed. In class, sketch a line flat at 10 m/s and ask how far the object travels in 5 seconds: the area under the flat line is 10 times 5, which is 50 metres - a stopped object travels nowhere.
trap.misconception: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped.

workedExample: A distance-time graph climbs in a straight line: 120 metres in 60 seconds. Speed = gradient = 120 / 60 = 2 m/s. Check the units: metres divided by seconds gives metres per second, and the straight line means that speed never changes.
